trust.identity: Derived from the server session; clients never select verified status, account ownership or purchased capabilities.
trust.capabilities: Array of scope strings for presentation only; every resource/state authorization is repeated on the server.
trust.hotmartWebhook: Backend-only endpoint. Not exposed through PlatformClient; requires configured HOTTOK, not student CSRF or cookie authentication.
trust.emailProof: A typed buyer email is not a login. The code must be delivered to and confirmed by its owner. No Hotmart password or SSO is implemented.

transport.origin: Exact configured origin; never derived from untrusted Host or arbitrary proxy headers.
transport.cors: No cross-origin browser access; no wildcard CORS.
transport.serviceWorker: Must not cache /api/, protected resources or authenticated responses.
transport.mutationCsrf: X-CSRF-Token, exactly 64 hexadecimal characters; required for browser POST including anonymous request/confirmation of a code.
transport.mutationOrigin: Reject cross-site mutations; validate the configured origin in addition to CSRF.

cookies.rotation: Confirming a code establishes a new authenticated cookie; client refreshes session metadata afterwards.

limits.rateLimits: Enforced by the server by email and actual connection origin; browser validation does not replace server limits.

rules: authenticated must be boolean.
Authenticated user requires id and email; anonymous user must be absent or null and capabilities empty.
capabilities is an array of scope strings, not an object.
Anonymous session context grants no course content.
Generic acceptance; no disclosure of existing enrollment.
The response never includes the OTP, session token or email content.
Code and challenge above are synthetic fixture values only.
Incorrect OTP uses HTTP422; preserve anonymous context and CSRF for a permitted retry. HTTP401 remains reserved for authentication expiry/absence and clears client context.
Server handles session cookie; client refreshes GET /session. No cookie/token in JSON.
Server revokes session; client always clears local private view state.
Network failure is not reported as successful server logout.

routes.response: Authorized bytes with configured safe MIME and private, no-store. No user-selected file path or grant.
rules: Unauthorized and missing resources are indistinguishable to the caller.
ID must match the resourceIdPattern; file keys and ownership are looked up server-side.
Playback/media integrations are separate; receiving legitimate bytes cannot prevent all copying.
data is an object or array, never null or a scalar.
Account ID comes only from the server session.
Atomic compare-and-save; conflict never causes a silent retry or overwrite.
data is an object or array within the UTF-8 limit.

routes.authentication: Configured X-HOTMART-HOTTOK validated by the backend.
rules: Persist validated events transactionally before acknowledgement.
No browser session or client-selected grant replaces event authentication.

clientFailureHandling.401: Clear private state, capabilities and CSRF; abort pending requests and require sign-in.
clientFailureHandling.403: Show access denied; no entitlement fallback.
clientFailureHandling.404: Generic unavailable resource result; do not reveal existence.
clientFailureHandling.409: Reload state before saving; do not retry automatically.
clientFailureHandling.422: Invalid OTP/input is rejected without clearing anonymous CSRF context; the user can retry within server limits. Do not treat this as a valid login.
clientFailureHandling.invalidPayload: Reject malformed payloads. Invalid session data clears private state.
clientFailureHandling.epoch: Responses begun before account clear/change cannot restore data, including delayed JSON/blob decoding.
clientFailureHandling.capabilityChange: Invalidate in-flight private state when refreshed scopes change.
clientFailureHandling.storage: No session credentials, OTP or grant authority stored in localStorage/sessionStorage.

testBoundary: The contract tests inject in-memory fetch/Response fixtures. They are client simulation only: no PHP execution, no HTTP server, no Node backend, no provider or production integration.
